newsitem.title: POLAND: McDonald's to continue fast Polish growth.
newsitem.headline: McDonald's to continue fast Polish growth.

text.p: The Polish unit of McDonald's Corp., McDonald's Polska Sp., plans to open several hundred restaurants in Poland by the year 2000, the company said in a statement Thursday.
The company also said it was launching a 250-million-zloty ($81 million) debt offering through a private placement of short-term and mid-term bonds to finance its further Polish expansion.
"The bond issue is to raise capital needed for further development in Poland," Francesca De Biase, chief finance director of McDonald's Polska, told a news conference.
McDonald's, which opened its first restaurant in Poland in 1992, now has 67 outlets in 33 cities and plans to open 30 new restaurants within the next year, the company's spokesman said.

Krzysztof Klapa said McDonald's Polska, which so far has invested more than $70 million in Poland, would invest another $28 million to $30 million in the next 12 months, continuing the company's fast expansion.
"McDonald's did not register such fast development as in Poland in any of 102 countries where it is present," Klapa said.
According to 1996 unaudited results, McDonald's Polska reported a net loss of 4.6 million zlotys ($1.49 million) on sales of 172.4 million zlotys ($56 million).
